title: Introduce network-graph-partitioner to cut Terraform plan latency
creator: Min-Jun Park
description:
Background: Some large environment plans (esp. when changing shared NAT / route table constructs) are taking 8–20+ minutes primarily due to a monolithic dependency graph traversal and repeated provider API calls. This impedes fast iteration for infra and slows automated canary rollouts.

Proposal: Add a lightweight 'network-graph-partitioner' that splits the Terraform graph into per-subgraph plan waves for networking resources (subnets, route tables, nat gateways, EIPs, transit attachments). The partitioner will: 1) identify edge subgraphs that touch only ephemeral resources, 2) schedule independent partitions concurrently, and 3) introduce a deterministic plan ordering to avoid thrashing provider calls. We'll ship as a thin adapter that lives in our infra tooling (not modifying core TF runtime) and plugs into our CI plan runner.

Goals:
- Reduce median plan time for large VPC changes by 40–60%
- Reduce provider API rate-limit risk during large rollouts
- Keep plan output and resource addresses stable (no churn)

Scope and out of scope:
- In scope: partitioner integration in CI, per-partition plan execution, state locking improvements to avoid long-held locks.
- Out of scope: full rewrite of terraform modules; we will not change resource names or move state between workspaces in this ticket.

Migration approach:
1) Add a feature-flagged partitioner in infra-ci-runner with a dry-run mode that emits partition plan report (no apply).
2) Run partitioner in dry-run across 10 representative workspaces (dev, staging, prod-sim) and audit drift.
3) Iterate provider call batching heuristics (max concurrent partitions, rate-limit backoff).
4) Enable partitioned plans for low-risk environments and run canaries on a single region.
5) Gradually enable for remaining workspaces after 2 weeks of monitoring.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Partitioning could reorder implicit dependencies and cause apply failures. Mitigation: conservative dependency detection, fail-open to single-plan if uncertainty detected.
- Risk: State-lock contention across partitions. Mitigation: short-lived locks per partition and central coordinator to serialize conflicting partitions.
- Risk: Interaction with provider upgrade (we'll be upgrading aws provider in parallel). Mitigation: coordinate with provider upgrade PR (see dependencies) and run combined smoke tests.

Acceptance criteria (must pass to mark Done):
- Partitioned plan reduces median plan time by >=40% on selected large workspaces (measured over 5 runs).
- No address churn introduced in state for any partitioned plan (verified by plan diffs).
- CI runner emits partitioning report and telemetry (partition sizes, time per partition, API calls).
- Rollout runbook and rollback steps documented in Confluence.

Operational checks & observability:
- Add partition-level tracing to Datadog (span per partition + provider API metrics).
- Alert on partition failure rate >2% and on lock wait longer than 30s.

Acceptance tests / validation plan:
- End-to-end: run partitioned plan against a cloned production workspace in test account, perform apply and verify network connectivity smoke tests.
- Load: synthetic plan runs in parallel to validate rate-limit backoff.
- Canary: enable partitioned plans for a low-risk team for 7 days and capture telemetry.

Rollout and rollback:
- Rollout will be gated by a feature-flag in infra-ci-runner. Initial rollout to dev/staging, then prod-sim, then production after monitoring window.
- Rollback: flip feature-flag off and re-run original monolithic plan path; we will keep last-good plan outputs to allow deterministic revert.

Implementation notes & key deliverables:
- Add new component infra-ci-runner/lib/partitioner (open-source style code in our infra repo).
- Add unit tests for partition detection heuristics and integration tests in infra-ci-runner/test/partitioner.
- Update terraform-runner pipeline to accept --partitions metadata and to emit partition reports.
- Coordinate AWS provider upgrade (4.62 -> 5.0) in dependent PR to ensure API compatibility for NAT/EIP lifecycle calls.

Estimated work items (rough):
- Design and prototype heuristics (2 spikes, 3d each)
- Implement partitioner adapter in infra-ci-runner (6d)
- Integration tests + telemetry (4d)
- Dry-run validation across 10 workspaces (3d)
- Gradual rollout and monitoring (5d)

Links and artifacts:
- Confluence design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INFRA/Network+Graph+Partitioner+Design
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-infra/infra-ci-runner/pull/618
- Related Linear: ENG-361482 (terraform-layering), ENG-41234 (state cleanup)
- Smoke test playbook: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1-example-smoke-playbook

updates: 2026-02-19: Kickoff meeting with Platform infra, Networking, and SRE. Agreed to conservative heuristics for first rollout.
2026-02-23: Spike 1 completed — heuristics prototype can split edge subgraphs for NAT/EIP changes without reordering route table dependencies in 8/10 test cases.
2026-02-28: Opened prototype PR to infra-ci-runner (PR #618). Prototype adds dry-run output and emits partition metrics to stdout.

2026-03-01: Ran dry-run across 5 staging workspaces; observed median plan time drop from 12m -> 6.8m (43% improvement). Two workspaces showed minor provider API throttling — tuning backoff in progress.
2026-03-03: Scheduled provider upgrade coordination meeting. Blocking tasks: finalize rate-limit backoff and add per-partition state lock window reduction.
